scenes.title: One Dollar and Eighty-Seven Cents
scenes.narration: One dollar and eighty-seven cents. That was all. And sixty cents of it was in copper pennies, saved one and two at a time whenever Della went to the grocer and the market. Three times Della counted the little stack of coins on the parlor table, and it was still one dollar and eighty-seven cents.

scenes.title: A Wistful Christmas Eve
scenes.narration: The very next day would be Christmas. Della sat quietly on the little floral settee in their upstairs parlor and sighed a soft, wistful sigh. She loved her husband Jim with all her heart, and she wanted so much to buy him a wonderful Christmas present.

scenes.title: Home in the Little Flat
scenes.narration: Della and Jim lived in a cozy, humble flat high up in an old brick house. Downstairs by the front door stood a tiny brass letter-box and a polished nameplate for James Dillingham Young. They did not have much money anymore, for Jim’s wages had grown smaller that winter. Yet every evening when Jim came up the stairs, Della met him at the door with the biggest, warmest hug in the world.

scenes.title: By the Frosty Window
scenes.narration: Della stood by the frosty parlor window and watched a fluffy grey cat walk along a snowy wooden fence in the yard below. For weeks she had dreamed of finding a gift for Jim that was fine, rare, and sterling — something truly worthy of her kind and hardworking husband. How could she ever find it for only one dollar and eighty-seven cents?

scenes.title: The Two Great Treasures
scenes.narration: Now, in Della and Jim’s house there were two treasures in which they both took a mighty pride. One was Jim’s shining gold pocket watch, which had belonged to his father and to his grandfather before him. The other was Della’s own glorious chestnut hair, which rippled and shone like a cascade of brown waters all the way past her waist.

She buttoned on her warm old brown winter coat, tied on her little brown hat, and hurried down the stairs into the snowy street.

scenes.title: Madame Sofronie’s Shop
scenes.narration: Down the street Della hurried until she reached the neat shop of Madame Sofronie, who bought and sold fine hair goods of all kinds. Della stepped up to the wooden counter, took off her hat, and asked if Madame Sofronie would buy her long brown hair. “Twenty dollars,” said Madame Sofronie kindly, admiring the rich brown tresses. — “Give it to me quick!” said Della with a brave smile.

scenes.title: Searching the Christmas Shops

The next two hours flew by as if on rosy wings! She went from shop to shop along the snowy avenues, peering into glowing Christmas windows to find the very best gift in the city for Jim.

scenes.title: The Platinum Watch Chain
scenes.narration: At last she found it in a quiet jeweler’s shop. It was a braided platinum fob chain for a pocket watch — simple, strong, and shining, with no gaudy ornaments at all. It was quiet and genuine, just like Jim. As soon as Della saw it, she knew it belonged on Jim’s grand gold watch. She paid twenty-one dollars for the chain and hurried home with eighty-seven cents left in her pocket.

scenes.title: “My Hair Is Sold and Gone”
scenes.narration: Della ran across the room and took Jim’s hands. “Jim, darling, don’t look at me that way! I had my hair cut off and sold it because I couldn’t have lived through Christmas without giving you a present. It’ll grow out again — and oh, Jim, wait till you see what I got for you!” At that, a warm, gentle smile spread across Jim’s face. He wrapped his arms around his Della and hugged her close, telling her that no haircut in the world could ever make him love his girl any less. Then he took the little paper-wrapped package from his coat and laid it on the table.

scenes.title: The Tortoiseshell Combs
scenes.narration: Della untied the string and unfolded the white paper — and then she gave a little gasp of pure joy! Resting inside were The Combs: the set of three tortoise-shell hair combs with sparkling jeweled rims that she had admired for months in a shop window on Broadway. They were the exact warm shade to wear in her vanished chestnut hair. Della hugged them to her heart and looked up at Jim with shining eyes. “Oh, they are so beautiful! And my hair grows awfully fast, Jim!”

scenes.title: Jim’s Secret Surprise
scenes.narration: Then Della jumped up and held out her own gift in her open palm, where the braided platinum chain flashed like pale silver in the lamplight. She asked Jim for his gold watch so they could see how handsome it looked together. Instead of reaching into his pocket, Jim sat down on the floral settee, leaned back, and smiled the warmest smile of all. “Dell, let’s put our Christmas presents away and keep them awhile. They’re too nice to use just at present. I sold the gold watch to get the money to buy your combs.”

scenes.title: The Wisest Gift-Givers of All
scenes.narration: Long ago, the Magi — the three wonderfully wise men — traveled beneath a bright star to bring the very first Christmas gifts. Some might say that Della and Jim were foolish to trade away the two greatest treasures of their house. Yet as they sat hand in hand in their warm little parlor while the snow fell outside, they had given each other something far greater than gold or jewels: their whole hearts. And of all who give and receive gifts anywhere in the world, such as they are the wisest. Everywhere they are the wisest. They are the Magi.
